[Bug] Refuse an input.audio System One rule on every deployment

## Purpose

Closes #6543. A System One decisions request carries no audio part, so no deployment reads one: the remote card reader already strips `audio` from a listed card (`systemOneDeployment.listedEntryCard`) and deployment capabilities refuse a card that declares it. But `checkAnswerer` checked `rule.Input.Media()` only against a known modality list, so an `input.audio` rule bound to a deployment with no card (an attached model runtime) loaded, decided on the text alone, and reported the input as scanned.

The answerer contract now refuses `input.audio` outright, with the established `input_modality_unsupported` wording naming the reason: no System One decisions request carries an audio part.

## Test Plan

```bash
cd src/semantic-router && go test ./pkg/config -run 'TestSystemOneAnswererLoadChecks|TestSystemOneRuleRefusesInputAudio' -count=1 && go test ./pkg/extproc -run TestARemoteDeploymentReadsOnlyTheModalitiesItsCardLists -count=1
```

- `TestSystemOneAnswererLoadChecks` gains `{audio, "attached"}` expecting `input_modality_unsupported`; `TestSystemOneRuleRefusesInputAudio` asserts the full refusal line against a card listing audio.
- The remote-card matrix keeps its audio rows and now asserts them through a loader that returns the load error (`moduleSystemOneRouterConfigTry`), since the refusal moved to load time.

## Test Result

On the previous revision the attached-deployment row loads (`got <nil>, want one line starting "recipes[...]input_modality_unsupported: "`); with the change every audio case refuses and the two packages pass in full (`./pkg/config` 2,627 cases, `./pkg/extproc` no failures).

fix(dashboard): keep what a webhook set when a full refresh settles after it

Closes #4108

## Why

A full refresh copies \`lastGood\` and the forge row before it computes, then wrote both back whole. A webhook that cleared the forge's failure mark in that window was undone. Every repo was fresh, but the forge read unreachable until the next webhook, and the next failed full refresh dated the rows from the older full read instead of the webhook's.

## What changed

- \`lastGood\` is merged per forge, keeping the later time, instead of assigned from the stale copy.
- When scoped refreshes newer than the full refresh have made every repo of a forge current, the full refresh no longer writes the failure mark back on the forge row (same \`clearMarkWhenFresh\` rule the scoped path uses).
- \`docs/live-updates.md\` says the overlap case holds.

## Tests

\`last_good_overlap_test.go\` holds a failing full refresh mid-compute through a source's \`ProviderStatus\` hook, runs both webhooks, then lets it settle. Channels order it, no sleeps. It pins that the forge stays reachable and that the next failure dates the rows from the webhooks. Both go red with the fix removed (checked for each half). The no-overlap case is covered by the existing carried-over tests, which pass. \`go test -race ./internal/dashboard\` is green.

The second commit is a lint follow-up to the first (an embedded type in two test literals).

#4106's follow-up list has no other overlap with this.

diff --git a/internal/dashboard/last_good_overlap_test.go b/internal/dashboard/last_good_overlap_test.go
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..8c900adf6
--- /dev/null
+++ b/internal/dashboard/last_good_overlap_test.go
@@ -0,0 +1,108 @@
+package dashboard_test
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"sync"
+	"testing"
+	"time"
+
+	"github.com/alrayyes/forge-dashboard/internal/dashboard"
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+)
+
+// pausingSource is a twoReposSource that can hold a failed full refresh in the
+// step after its fetch has returned, where the refresh computes its snapshot
+// from copies it took earlier. A scoped refresh run while it holds lands in
+// the window #4108 describes.
+type pausingSource struct {
+	twoReposSource
+	pauseMu sync.Mutex
+	entered chan struct{}
+	release chan struct{}
+}
+
+// pauseNext makes the next failed full refresh stop and wait, and returns the
+// channel that says it has stopped and the one that lets it go on.
+func (s *pausingSource) pauseNext() (<-chan struct{}, func()) {
+	s.pauseMu.Lock()
+	defer s.pauseMu.Unlock()
+	entered, released := make(chan struct{}), make(chan struct{})
+	s.entered, s.release = entered, released
+
+	return entered, func() { close(released) }
+}
+
+func (s *pausingSource) ProviderStatus(context.Context) *dashboard.ProviderStatus {
+	s.pauseMu.Lock()
+	entered, release := s.entered, s.release
+	s.entered, s.release = nil, nil
+	s.pauseMu.Unlock()
+	if entered != nil {
+		close(entered)
+		<-release
+	}
+
+	return nil
+}
+
+// refreshWhileFullRefreshComputes fails a full refresh, then runs a second
+// one that fails too and holds it mid-compute while webhooks refresh both repos.
+// It returns the time the second one's failure was dated from, once it has
+// settled.
+func refreshWhileFullRefreshComputes(t *testing.T, agg *dashboard.Aggregator, src *pausingSource) (fullReadAt time.Time) {
+	t.Helper()
+	agg.Refresh(t.Context())
+	src.goDown()
+	agg.Refresh(t.Context())
+	fullReadAt = *health(agg.Get(), dashboard.ForgeGitHub).StaleSince
+
+	entered, release := src.pauseNext()
+	done := make(chan struct{})
+	go func() {
+		defer close(done)
+		agg.Refresh(t.Context())
+	}()
+	<-entered
+	require.True(t, agg.RefreshRepo(t.Context(), dashboard.ForgeGitHub, "o", "a", "o/a"))
+	require.True(t, agg.RefreshRepo(t.Context(), dashboard.ForgeGitHub, "o", "b", "o/b"))
+	require.True(t, health(agg.Get(), dashboard.ForgeGitHub).Reachable)
+	release()
+	<-done
+
+	return fullReadAt
+}
+
+// A webhook that clears the forge's mark while a failing full refresh is still
+// computing is not undone when that refresh settles (#4108).
+func TestAggregator_AFullRefreshSettlingAfterWebhooksClearedTheForge_KeepsItReachable(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+	src := &pausingSource{forge: dashboard.ForgeGitHub}
+	agg := dashboard.NewAggregator([]dashboard.Source{src})
+
+	refreshWhileFullRefreshComputes(t, agg, src)
+
+	h := health(agg.Get(), dashboard.ForgeGitHub)
+	assert.True(t, h.Reachable)
+	assert.Nil(t, h.StaleSince)
+	assert.Empty(t, h.Error)
+	assert.Nil(t, repoNamed(t, agg, "o/a").StaleSince)
+	assert.Nil(t, repoNamed(t, agg, "o/b").StaleSince)
+}
+
+// The webhooks' read time outlives the full refresh that settled after them, so
+// the next failure dates the rows from the webhooks, not the older full read.
+func TestAggregator_AFullRefreshSettlingAfterWebhooksClearedTheForge_KeepsTheLaterGoodTime(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+	src := &pausingSource{forge: dashboard.ForgeGitHub}
+	agg := dashboard.NewAggregator([]dashboard.Source{src})
+	fullReadAt := refreshWhileFullRefreshComputes(t, agg, src)
+
+	agg.Refresh(t.Context())
+
+	for _, name := range []string{"o/a", "o/b"} {
+		since := repoNamed(t, agg, name).StaleSince
+		require.NotNil(t, since, name)
+		assert.True(t, since.After(fullReadAt), "%s is dated from the webhook, not the last full read", name)
+	}
+}

emu: 客体时钟源一直用 TSC（tsc=nowatchdog）

Refs ModAVD/ModAVD#110

## 问题

一台连续开了约 14 小时的实例（明日方舟 + MAA）突然变得很卡：游戏从 55–60 fps 掉到约 5 fps，而且一直卡到下次冷启动。

现场采样：

- 游戏渲染线程 `UnityGfxDeviceWorker` 占满一个核，其中约 90% 是内核态；simpleperf 里 `read_hpet` 占 72%，`goldfish_address_space` 的 `as_ioctl` 占 14%。
- 宿主显卡（qemu 的 3D 约 4%）和宿主的渲染线程都很闲；客体内存没有回收压力。
- 客体时钟源已经从 `tsc` 换成了 `hpet`。内核日志：

```
clocksource: timekeeping watchdog on CPU4: hpet read-back delay of 209700ns, attempt 3, marking unstable
tsc: Marking TSC unstable due to clocksource watchdog
clocksource: Switched to clocksource hpet
```

这正好是 #110 列出的第三种原因：运行中看门狗读 hpet 太慢。WHPX 不给客体 kvm-clock，tsc 一停用就只剩 QEMU 模拟的 hpet，之后每次读时钟都要退出到宿主。看门狗用 hpet 校验 tsc，主机一忙，读一次 hpet 就可能超过门限，连续三次超时就会停用 tsc。那次开机的 14 小时里，客体记了 78 次 hpet 读得慢，第 13.8 小时连续三次没过。所以开得越久，越早会碰上。

客体 CPU 报了 `constant_tsc` 和 `nonstop_tsc`，但没有 `tsc_adjust`。6.1 内核要三个都有才会自动让 TSC 免检，所以看门狗一直在检查 TSC。

## 改动

Windows 上给客体内核加 `tsc=nowatchdog`（通过 `-qemu -append`，模拟器会把它合并进内核命令行，不会替换原有参数）。

- 它只是让看门狗不再检查 TSC；开机时的各核 TSC 同步检查照做，真的不同步还是会被发现。
- 没用 `tsc=reliable`：那个连同步检查也一起跳过。以前在没修 TSC 的模拟器上用过它，`system_server` 读到时间倒退后崩溃了。
- macOS（ARM64）和 Linux（KVM，有 kvm-clock）不加。

## 测试

- `go test ./internal/emu/...` 通过；`TestBuildLaunchArgs` 两张参考表都加上了 `-append tsc=nowatchdog`。
- 变异检查：把这行去掉以后 `TestBuildLaunchArgs` 失败，恢复后通过。
- 实机（Windows 11 + WHPX，0.41.1 的模拟器，测试根）：用这个分支的命令行开机，`/proc/cmdline` 里有 `tsc=nowatchdog`，原有参数都还在，时钟源是 `tsc`；开明日方舟跑到主界面，没有新的崩溃（只有一直都有的 `com.google.android.bluetooth` SIGABRT），关机正常。
- 长时间运行和多游戏放到发版回归一起测。

fix(web): keep a multi-select panel open while a row is pressed

Closes #4093

## Why

On a phone, clicking the name of a choice in the Repo, Author or Label filter did nothing. Only the checkbox itself ticked. Each row is already one label around its box, so the label was never the problem.

The Filters sheet scrolls on a phone. Pressing a row's name moves focus to the nearest focusable ancestor, which is the sheet, outside the panel. The panel's `focusout` handler took that for the reader leaving and closed the panel on pointerdown. The click then landed on whatever sat under the closed panel, so nothing ticked. The box worked because it takes focus inside the panel. Desktop was never affected: no focusable ancestor there.

## What changed

`focusout` is ignored while a pointer press that started inside the panel is still down. Tabbing out and clicking elsewhere still close it.

`tests/pick-row-click.spec.ts` covers the name, the row's padding, the 20-pick cap, Tab and Space, and axe in light and dark, at desktop and phone width. It was red on the phone before the fix (name, padding and cap tests), green after.

## Tests

- `pick-row-click`, `filter-pick-panel-focus`, `label-multi-select`, `repo-author-multi-select`, `mobile-filters` Playwright specs: 103 passed
- `tsc` over the tests and `biome check` on the touched files: clean
